rca_reporting_template.overview: Comprehensive template for creating Root Cause Analysis (RCA) reports that document incident investigations. This template ensures all critical information is captured in a clear, actionable format for stakeholders, engineering teams, and future reference.

section.name: executive_summary
section.purpose: Provide a concise overview for stakeholders who need to understand the incident without technical details

content_guidelines.guideline: State what happened, when, impact, and root cause
Focus on business impact and resolution

section.template:
## Executive Summary
On [DATE] at [TIME], [SERVICE/APPLICATION] experienced [INCIDENT TYPE] that resulted in [IMPACT]. The incident lasted [DURATION] and affected [SCOPE]. The root cause was identified as [ROOT CAUSE IN SIMPLE TERMS]. The issue has been resolved by [RESOLUTION], and preventive measures have been implemented to avoid recurrence.
section.example:
## Executive Summary
On March 15, 2026 at 14:23 UTC, the Payment Service experienced intermittent failures that resulted in 15% of payment transactions failing. The incident lasted 2 hours and 17 minutes, affecting approximately 3,500 customers. The root cause was identified as a memory leak in the user session cache causing pods to crash. The issue has been resolved by implementing cache eviction policies, and monitoring has been enhanced to detect similar issues early.

subsection.name: impact_assessment
subsection.description: Quantify the business and technical impact
subsection.template:
## Impact Assessment
**Duration:** 2 hours 17 minutes (14:23 - 16:40 UTC)
**Affected Services:** - Payment Service (complete outage for 25 minutes) - Order Processing (degraded performance)
**User Impact:** - Approximately 3,500 customers affected - 15% of payment transactions failed (523 out of 3,487) - Average latency increased from 200ms to 2,500ms
**Business Impact:** - Estimated $45,000 in failed transactions - 127 customer support tickets created - SLO breach: 99.9% availability target missed (actual: 98.7%)
**Technical Impact:** - 3 pods OOMKilled and restarted - 15 pod restarts total during incident - Database connection pool temporarily exhausted

subsection.name: detection_and_response
subsection.description: How the incident was detected and initial response
subsection.template:
## Detection and Response
**Detection:** - Incident detected by Instana alert "High Error Rate - Payment Service" at 14:23:15 UTC - Alert triggered when error rate exceeded 5% threshold - On-call engineer paged via PagerDuty at 14:23:30 UTC
**Initial Response:** - On-call engineer acknowledged alert at 14:24:00 UTC - Checked Instana dashboard for error patterns - Identified pod crashes in OpenShift - Escalated to platform team at 14:35:00 UTC - War room established at 14:45:00 UTC
**Response Time:** - Time to detection: < 1 minute (automated) - Time to acknowledgment: 45 seconds - Time to mitigation: 1 hour 57 minutes - Time to resolution: 2 hours 17 minutes

section.name: root_cause_analysis
section.purpose: Provide detailed technical analysis of the root cause

subsection.name: symptoms_observed
subsection.description: Document all symptoms identified during investigation
subsection.template:
## Symptoms Observed
### Instana Observations - Error rate spiked from 0.1% to 15% at 14:23:15 UTC - Latency P99 increased from 500ms to 8,000ms - Heap memory usage showed steady increase over 6 hours before crash - GC pause times increased from 50ms to 2,000ms - Traces showed "OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space" in multiple spans
### OpenShift Observations - Pods terminated with Exit Code 137 (OOMKilled) - Pod events showed "Killing container with id docker://abc123 due to OOMKilled" - Memory usage at 100% of limit (2Gi) before crashes - 15 pod restarts across 3 replicas - No CPU throttling observed
### Application Logs ``` 2026-03-15 14:25:29.847 ERROR [payment-service] OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space 2026-03-15 14:25:29.848 ERROR [payment-service] at java.util.HashMap.resize(HashMap.java:704) 2026-03-15 14:25:29.849 ERROR [payment-service] at com.example.UserSessionCache.put(UserSessionCache.java:45) ```

subsection.name: investigation_process
subsection.description: Document the investigation steps and hypotheses considered
subsection.template:
## Investigation Process
### Hypotheses Considered
**Hypothesis 1: Memory leak in application code** - Supporting Evidence: - Heap usage steadily increasing over time in Instana - OOMKilled pods with Exit Code 137 - No memory leak in previous version - Contradicting Evidence: None - Conclusion: **CONFIRMED** - Root cause identified
**Hypothesis 2: Insufficient memory limits** - Supporting Evidence: - Pods hitting memory limit - Contradicting Evidence: - Memory limit (2Gi) was adequate for previous versions - Heap usage pattern shows leak, not just high usage - Conclusion: **REFUTED** - Symptom, not root cause
**Hypothesis 3: External service causing memory pressure** - Supporting Evidence: None - Contradicting Evidence: - External service response times normal - No correlation with external service calls - Conclusion: **REFUTED** - No evidence
### Investigation Steps 1. Analyzed Instana metrics showing heap growth pattern 2. Examined OpenShift pod events confirming OOMKills 3. Retrieved pod logs showing OutOfMemoryError stack traces 4. Analyzed heap dump (obtained before crash) showing 1.8GB of UserSession objects 5. Reviewed code changes in recent deployment 6. Identified unbounded HashMap in UserSessionCache.java added in v2.3.0 7. Confirmed cache had no eviction policy or size limit

subsection.name: root_cause
subsection.description: State the root cause clearly with supporting evidence
subsection.template:
## Root Cause
**Root Cause:** Unbounded cache in UserSessionCache causing memory leak
**Location:** `src/main/java/com/example/cache/UserSessionCache.java:45`
**Defect Description:** The UserSessionCache class uses an unbounded HashMap to store user session objects. The cache was introduced in version 2.3.0 (deployed March 15, 2026 at 08:00 UTC) to improve performance by caching user session data. However, the implementation lacks any eviction policy or size limit.
**Problematic Code:** ```java public class UserSessionCache { private static final Map<String, UserSession> cache = new HashMap<>();
public void put(String userId, UserSession session) { cache.put(userId, session); // No eviction, grows unbounded }
public UserSession get(String userId) { return cache.get(userId); } } ```
**Causal Chain:** 1. UserSessionCache accumulates UserSession objects for every unique user login 2. Each UserSession object is approximately 2KB in size 3. Cache never evicts entries, growing indefinitely 4. After ~900,000 unique user logins (over 6 hours), heap exhausted 5. JVM throws OutOfMemoryError 6. Pod killed by Kubernetes with OOMKilled status 7. Pod restarts, temporarily resolving issue 8. Pattern repeats, causing recurring outages
**Evidence:** - Heap dump analysis showed 1.8GB (90% of heap) consumed by HashMap entries - 897,432 UserSession objects in cache at time of crash - Code review confirmed no eviction policy in UserSessionCache - Git history shows cache added in commit abc123 on March 14, 2026 - No similar issues in version 2.2.0 (before cache was added)

subsection.name: contributing_factors
subsection.description: Identify factors that contributed to or exacerbated the issue
subsection.template:
## Contributing Factors
While the root cause was the unbounded cache, several factors contributed to the severity and duration of the incident:
1. **Insufficient Code Review** - Cache implementation not reviewed for memory management - No discussion of eviction policy in pull request
2. **Missing Monitoring** - No alerts on heap usage trends - Cache size not exposed as metric - No heap dump collection on OOMKill
3. **Inadequate Testing** - Load testing did not run long enough to expose leak - No memory leak detection in CI/CD pipeline - Performance tests only ran for 30 minutes (leak takes 6+ hours)
4. **Deployment Timing** - Deployed during business hours - No gradual rollout (canary deployment) - All pods updated simultaneously
5. **Delayed Detection** - Heap growth was gradual (6 hours to failure) - No proactive monitoring of heap trends - First alert only triggered after errors started

section.name: resolution
section.purpose: Document how the issue was resolved
section.template:
## Resolution
### Immediate Fix (Deployed 16:20 UTC)
Modified UserSessionCache to use Guava Cache with eviction policy:
```java public class UserSessionCache { private static final Cache<String, UserSession> cache = CacheBuilder.newBuilder() .maximumSize(10000) // Limit to 10,000 entries .expireAfterWrite(1, TimeUnit.HOURS) // Expire after 1 hour .expireAfterAccess(30, TimeUnit.MINUTES) // Expire if not accessed .recordStats() // Enable cache statistics .build();
public void put(String userId, UserSession session) { cache.put(userId, session); }
public UserSession get(String userId) { return cache.getIfPresent(userId); } } ```
**Changes Made:** - Replaced HashMap with Guava Cache - Added maximum size limit (10,000 entries) - Added time-based eviction (1 hour write, 30 min access) - Enabled cache statistics for monitoring
**Deployment:** - Fix deployed as hotfix version 2.3.1 - Gradual rollout: 1 pod → 2 pods → all pods - Monitored heap usage during rollout - Confirmed stable memory usage after deployment
### Verification
Post-deployment metrics (16:40 - 18:00 UTC): - Heap usage stable at 45% (900MB of 2GB) - No pod restarts - Error rate returned to baseline (0.1%) - Latency P99 returned to 500ms - Cache hit rate: 87% - Cache evictions: ~100 per minute (expected)

section.name: preventive_measures
section.purpose: Document actions to prevent recurrence and improve processes

category.name: immediate_actions
category.description: Actions taken immediately to prevent recurrence
category.template:
## Preventive Measures
### Immediate Actions (Completed)
1. **Enhanced Monitoring** - Added Instana alert for heap usage > 70% for 10 minutes - Exposed cache metrics (size, hit rate, evictions) to Prometheus - Created dashboard for cache monitoring - Configured heap dump collection on OOMKill
2. **Code Review** - Reviewed all other cache implementations in codebase - Identified 3 other unbounded caches, created tickets to fix - Updated code review checklist to include cache eviction policies
3. **Documentation** - Documented cache best practices in engineering wiki - Added cache implementation guidelines to coding standards - Created runbook for memory leak investigation

category.name: short_term_actions
category.description: Actions to be completed within 1-2 weeks
category.template:
### Short-term Actions (1-2 weeks)
1. **Testing Improvements** - Extend load testing duration to 12 hours minimum - Add memory leak detection to CI/CD pipeline - Implement automated heap dump analysis - Add cache-specific performance tests
2. **Deployment Process** - Implement mandatory canary deployments for production - Add automated rollback on error rate increase - Require deployment during off-peak hours for high-risk changes
3. **Monitoring Enhancements** - Add proactive alerts for heap growth trends - Implement anomaly detection for memory usage - Create SLO for memory usage stability

category.name: long_term_actions
category.template:
### Long-term Actions (1-3 months)
1. **Architecture Review** - Evaluate distributed caching solution (Redis, Memcached) - Design cache strategy for microservices - Implement cache warming strategies
2. **Process Improvements** - Establish memory management review board - Create cache design review process - Implement regular memory profiling in production
3. **Training** - Conduct training on memory management best practices - Share RCA findings in engineering all-hands - Create cache implementation workshop
4. **Tooling** - Implement automated cache configuration validation - Create cache sizing calculator tool - Build cache monitoring dashboard template

section.name: lessons_learned
section.purpose: Capture key learnings for the organization
section.template:
## Lessons Learned
### What Went Well
1. **Rapid Detection** - Automated monitoring detected issue within 1 minute - Alert routing worked correctly
2. **Effective Collaboration** - War room established quickly - Cross-team collaboration (SRE, Dev, Platform) - Clear communication with stakeholders
3. **Systematic Investigation** - Followed structured RCA process - Gathered evidence from multiple sources - Validated root cause before implementing fix
### What Could Be Improved
1. **Prevention** - Cache implementation should have been reviewed more thoroughly - Load testing duration was insufficient - No proactive heap monitoring
2. **Detection** - Should have detected heap growth trend before OOMKills - Need better visibility into cache behavior
3. **Response** - Took too long to identify root cause (1h 52m) - Could have used heap dumps earlier in investigation - Rollback strategy not clearly defined
### Key Takeaways
1. **Always implement eviction policies for caches** - Never use unbounded collections for caching - Consider size limits, time-based eviction, and LRU policies - Monitor cache metrics (size, hit rate, evictions)
2. **Extend load testing duration** - Memory leaks may take hours to manifest - Test for at least 12 hours under realistic load - Monitor memory trends during testing
3. **Proactive monitoring is critical** - Don't wait for failures to alert - Monitor trends and anomalies - Alert on concerning patterns before they cause outages
4. **Code review must include resource management** - Review all cache implementations - Check for resource leaks (connections, memory, threads) - Validate configuration (limits, timeouts, pool sizes)
